newsitem.title: USA: Alabama income tax revenues drop nine pct in Aug.
newsitem.headline: Alabama income tax revenues drop nine pct in Aug.

text.p: Alabama income tax revenues dropped to $171.3 million in August, a decrease of nine percent from August 1995, state Revenue Department reported.
State officials said they had not determined whether the decrease was due to late filing or whether it represented an actual decline.

But they said the economy was still strong, unemployment was at its lowest in more than 20 years, and sales tax revenues were still rising. Income tax revenue for the first 11 months of the fiscal year were 6.5 percent above the same period last year.
State Budget Officer Bill Newton said overall state revenues were not growing as fast as last year, largely because the state legislature lowered the premium tax insurance companies pay.
State revenue has increased about 2.4 percent over last year. The growth rate had been more than eight percent before the insurance premium tax was lowered.
